title: Object card
hint: A click on a source in the image shows what is known about it.
noCatalog: There is no Gaia data for this field yet.

distance.rough: It is roughly {{lightYears}} light-years away: its parallax is very small and the measurement has a wide margin.
distance.far: It is too far to measure its distance: more than {{lightYears}} light-years away.
distance.none: Gaia could not measure its distance.

light.measured: This light left about {{years}} years ago.
light.rough: This light left about {{years}} years ago, give or take.
light.far: This light left more than {{years}} years ago.

motion.moving: It moves {{rate}} per year toward the {{direction}}. At that pace it takes about {{years}} years to cross the width of the full Moon.
motion.still: Gaia finds no motion across the sky.
motion.none: Gaia could not measure its motion.
motion.velocity: At that distance it is about {{speed}} km/s across the sky.

brightness.nakedEye: In visible light its magnitude is {{magnitude}}: it can be seen with the naked eye under a dark sky.
brightness.binoculars: In visible light its magnitude is {{magnitude}}: it can be seen with binoculars.
brightness.smallTelescope: In visible light its magnitude is {{magnitude}}: it takes an amateur telescope.
brightness.largeTelescope: In visible light its magnitude is {{magnitude}}: only large telescopes reach it.

empty.title: Gaia has no source at this point
empty.radius: There is none within {{radius}} of this point.
empty.nearby: The nearest one is {{distance}} away, at magnitude {{magnitude}}. If the click was meant for that star, the button shows it.
empty.why: Gaia measures visible light. A very cold object hardly emits there, even if it shines in the infrared: that is why it can show up in WISE and SPHEREx and be missing from Gaia. That is the case of WISE 0855, the coldest brown dwarf known.
empty.other: It can also be a distant galaxy, part of a nebula or an image defect.
